references.text: Describes how the flood actually happened, and how all flesh that had the breath of life in its nostrils, everything on dry land, died.
God tells Noah that He has decided to put an end to all flesh, for the earth is full of violence. The immediate context for God's announcement of the flood.
God announces that in seven days He will send rain on the earth for forty days and forty nights, and wipe out every creature He has made.
The Lord sat enthroned over the flood; the Lord sits as king forever. Shows God's sovereignty over the flood.
By faith Noah, being warned about things not yet seen, in reverence prepared an ark to save his family. This verse refers to Noah's actions based on God's warning about the flood.
God did not spare the ancient world, but preserved Noah, a preacher of righteousness, along with seven others, when He brought the flood upon a world of ungodly people.
Jesus compares His return to the days of Noah, when people were eating and drinking and knew nothing until the flood came and took them all away.
Strong theological parallel: God's decision to wipe out all flesh from the face of the earth.
Strong parallel in the expression about completely wiping out everything from the face of the earth.
Direct covenant connection: The promise that the flood will never happen again.
Theological cause-and-effect: Sin introduced death, which led to the flood.
Theological context: The flood as a concrete manifestation of God's wrath against ungodliness.
Direct covenant connection: The promise that the flood will never happen again.
